issues.description: The problem statement refers to an error-detection function named `_detect_errors(...)` (returns 1 when no error is detected), but both the template and the solution implement the function as `detect_errors(...)` (no leading underscore). This name mismatch in the specification vs. code can confuse students about which function to implement and what tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the function name across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either (a) update the problem statement to refer to `detect_errors(...)` (no leading underscore) and clarify its return semantics, or (b) rename the function in the template and solution to `_detect_errors(...)`. Ensure the tests and all references use the same exact name.

issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_detect_errors(...)`, but both the template and the solution define and use the function named `detect_errors(...)` (no leading underscore). This mismatch of a single leading underscore for the same conceptual routine may confuse students about which function to implement or test against.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier across all artifacts. Either (a) update problem_statement.md to request `detect_errors(...)` (remove the leading underscore), or (b) add a thin wrapper `_detect_errors = detect_errors` in the template and solution so both names resolve to the same implementation. Prefer (a) for clarity.
